findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() uses unwrap() on fallible I/O
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable file panics the caller instead of returning a typed error (e.g. Io/Parse)
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, E> and propagate with ? or map_err; do not unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() uses unwrap() on fallible parse
findings.failure_mode: Malformed line (non-numeric second field) panics instead of returning a typed Parse/Decode error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| Error::Parse(...))? on a safely-indexed field

findings.problem: Lossy as cast from u32 to u16: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16
findings.failure_mode: Values > 65535 silently truncate, corrupting data silently without error
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 (parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>()) and propagate errors via Result; never use lossy as for width narrowing

findings.problem: Unreachable! implied by unchecked parts[0] indexing after split (no bounds check)
findings.failure_mode: Empty or single-field lines cause index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly two fields, or parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with ? propagation

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: Empty line or missing first field causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') which returns Option<(&str, &str)>, match on Some/None to handle missing fields

findings.problem: Hidden side effect: println!() inside data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: I/O logging leaks into the data-loading function, making pure parsing non-deterministic and untestable; pollutes stdout in library consumers
findings.fix: Remove println!; log only in the imperative shell layer (caller side), keep core pure

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; allocates N Strings for a two-field record; violates bounded-allocation discipline
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (&str, &str) without intermediate Vec or String allocations

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println) with pure parsing in one function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot test parsing logic independently of file system; side effects make the core impure and brittle
findings.fix: Split into (1) load_sessions_raw(path) -> Result<String, E> for I/O and (2) parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> for pure parsing

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper despite multiple fallible operations
findings.failure_mode: Caller has no way to distinguish success from failure; all errors manifest as panics
findings.fix: Change signature to fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> or a domain-specific Error enum

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() then as u16 wastes arithmetic checks; no overflow guard before width narrowing
findings.failure_mode: Values in [65536, u32::MAX] silently wrap to u16 range without error
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16; the parser natively rejects out-of-range values and returns an error

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (criterion, perf, or flamegraph) for the parsing hot path
no allocation tracking (e.g. mimalloc stats or dlmalloc counters) for per-line Vec<String> overhead
no command-line evidence (cargo test / cargo clippy output) was produced for this review
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All 10 findings are BLOCKERs. The crate has zero type safety on external input, uses unwrap on every fallible boundary, has a lossy cast, leaks I/O into core logic, and allocates unboundedly per line. A full repair would require: (1) Result-returning signature, (2) split_once parsing, (3) parse::<u16> directly, (4) no println in core, (5) try_reserve on the output Vec, (6) removal of all unwrap/panic/as casts. Residual risk is high until all blockers are resolved and evidence is produced.
